props.title: It Happened Here
props.initialSlug: A shocking vision of a chilling future.

sections.content: **It Happened Here (1966)** (1966) stands as one of the most chilling alternate history films ever made. Shot over 8 years by amateur filmmakers Kevin Brownlow and Andrew Mollo when they were teenagers, this groundbreaking mockumentary imagines Nazi-occupied Britain in 1944. The film's documentary-style realism was so convincing that many viewers thought they were watching actual Nazi footage. It pairs naturally with **The World in My Corner** (1956) and **The Man in the High Castle** (2015-2019) in exploring how fascism could take root in English-speaking nations. The film's most controversial scenes featured real British fascists expressing their views - sequences initially cut by the British Board of Film Censors.

sections.content: The film's influence can be seen in later alternate history works like **SS-GB** (2017) and **An Englishman's Castle** (1978), both BBC productions exploring similar "what if" scenarios of Nazi victory. But **It Happened Here** distinguishes itself through its unflinching documentary approach and use of real locations, including actual wartime buildings and equipment. The amateur cast, mostly consisting of non-actors, adds to the film's unsettling authenticity.

Most remarkable is how the film examines collaboration not through melodrama but through mundane daily choices. Lead actress Pauline Murray's performance as nurse Pauline captures the gradual normalization of fascism through small compromises. This approach influenced later works like The Pianist (2002) and The Grey Zone (2001) in their examination of survival under totalitarianism. SUBHEAD: Technical Innovation and Historical Impact

sections.content: The film's technical achievements cannot be overstated. Working with virtually no budget, Brownlow and Mollo created convincing 1940s period detail through meticulous research and borrowed uniforms and equipment. Their attention to detail influenced later historical productions like **Downfall** (2004) and **Come and See** (1985) in their pursuit of absolute historical accuracy. The film's mix of documentary and narrative techniques paved the way for later mockumentaries like **Death of a President** (2006).
